s1.syndrome_frame: Postoperative corneal inflammation with deep stromal involvement
salient_findings: Keratitis in the right eye two months after DSAEK
Brown, multilobular lesions in the deep corneal stroma
Central infiltrate involving all corneal layers on optical coherence tomography
key_facts: 68-year-old man with pseudophakic bullous keratopathy
Underwent DSAEK in the right eye
History of eye infection by Thaumetopoea pityocampa 9 months before DSAEK
Postoperative course was initially uneventful under topical and systemic corticosteroids
Best-corrected visual acuity was 20/200 in the right eye
Pupils were isocoric and isoreactive without an afferent pupillary defect
No pain with ocular movements
Slit-lamp biomicroscopy showed brown, multilobular lesions in the deep corneal stroma
Anterior chamber was deep and clear
Intraocular pressure and fundus examination were normal

shortlist.label: Fungal keratitis
shortlist.why_kept: Brown, multilobular lesions in the deep corneal stroma are consistent with fungal infection

shortlist.label: Acanthamoeba keratitis
shortlist.why_kept: History of contact lens use is not mentioned, but Acanthamoeba keratitis can occur in non-contact lens wearers, especially with a history of trauma or exposure to contaminated water

shortlist.label: Herpes simplex keratitis
shortlist.why_kept: Keratitis with deep stromal involvement can be caused by herpes simplex virus, especially in the context of recent surgery

shortlist.label: Candida keratitis
shortlist.why_kept: Fungal keratitis is a known complication of corneal surgery, and Candida is a common cause of postoperative fungal keratitis

shortlist.label: Aspergillus keratitis
shortlist.why_kept: Aspergillus is a common cause of fungal keratitis, especially in the context of trauma or surgery, and can cause deep stromal lesions

raw.rationale: The presence of brown, multilobular lesions in the deep corneal stroma, as seen on slit-lamp biomicroscopy, is more characteristic of fungal keratitis, which often presents with distinct infiltrates and can have a history of preceding ocular trauma or surgery, such as DSAEK.

rejected.label: Acanthamoeba keratitis
rejected.why: Acanthamoeba keratitis typically presents with severe pain, photophobia, and characteristic ring-shaped infiltrates, which are not mentioned in the case description.
